strengths: Novel mechanistic interpretability approach to spatial relation generation in diffusion transformers, addressing an understudied aspect of T2I models
Well-motivated 'Attention Synopsis' method for analyzing massive attention tensors (10M+ maps) at scale—practical contribution for mechanistic interpretability research
Rigorous experimental design with controlled synthetic dataset, multiple model scales, and multiple text encoder configurations enabling clean comparisons

Comprehensive evidence for findings: attention patterns, QK/VO circuit analysis, ablations (L2H8 ablation: 67→33%, L4H3 ablation: 90→76%), causal interventions (VO injection), training dynamics, and variance partitioning
Clear contrast between RTE and T5 circuits with distinct mechanistic explanations (two-stage modular vs. information fusion)
Strong reproducibility: extensive appendices with pseudocode, hyperparameters, detailed methods, and commitment to release code/data
Honest acknowledgment of limitations and presentation of robustness findings (40% drop from perturbation) without overstating generality
weaknesses: Severe scope limitations undermine generalization claims: only 2 objects (real scenes have 5+), 8 directional relations only, tiny models (DiT-B is 12 layers), synthetic only, low resolution (128×128). Enormous gap to real T2I systems (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion); no empirical validation that findings transfer.

Main practical finding—'text encoders matter for spatial reasoning'—was already known from cited work [33, 17]. Mechanistic explanation is new but actionable insight is not. Suggestion that 'encoder improvements > DiT modifications' is speculative without real-model experiments.

T5-DiT mechanism incompletely explained: why does adding 'the' cause catastrophic failure (40% drop)? Variance partitioning shows relation info (~12-21%) is present, but how it's used downstream is unclear. Why don't RTE models suffer similarly?

Limited architectural exploration: only one architecture (PixArt), only two text encoders (T5, random). Real T2I uses diverse designs (CLIP, hybrids). Findings may be artifacts of PixArt rather than general properties.

Robustness evaluation too narrow: only one perturbation type tested (adding 'the'). Should test paraphrasing, synonyms, reordering. The 40% drop is isolated; no analysis of which components cause fragility.

QK circuit explanation lacks rigor: composite relation decomposition (Fig 4B) shown qualitatively; unclear if exact or approximate. 'Gradient tagging' analogy is informal; mathematical formalism needed.

Incomplete ablations: no hybrid models (RTE with T5-style fusion, vice versa), no attempts to improve T5-DiT robustness, limited lesioning studies. DiT-nano failure (5%) unexplained—capacity threshold?
Evaluation concerns: binary contour-detection metrics may miss spatial understanding; no human evaluation. Single injection example (Fig 5C) generalized without showing consistency across prompts.

strengths: Novel Attention Synopsis method for aggregating and analyzing millions of cross-attention maps, with potential utility for diffusion model interpretability studies
Clear identification of two-stage circuit in RTE-based DiTs with well-supported QK/VO component analysis, providing interpretable mechanistic insights
Rigorous multi-method validation combining attention analysis, ablations (L2H8 34% drop, L4H3 14% drop), causal interventions (VO injection), and representation analysis
Interesting finding that T5 encodes relational information within object tokens rather than via explicit relation words, validated through variance partitioning and vector arithmetic
Systematic comparison across model scales (nano to B) and text encoder variants demonstrating scope of findings, plus identification of robustness differences to perturbations
Comprehensive experimental documentation including dataset construction pseudocode, hyperparameters, and extensive appendices supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Severely limited task domain (2 objects, 3 shapes, 2 colors, 8 relations, 128×128 images, gray background)—orders of magnitude simpler than realistic compositional generation; generalization to 3+ objects, complex occlusions, longer prompts, high resolution, diverse vocabularies completely unexamined

Unclear practical relevance for real T2I spatial generation: no connection demonstrated to actual failure modes (Fig. 10), no evidence these circuits exist in production models, and no downstream task improvements from findings

T5-DiT analysis less convincing than RTE-DiT—absence of clear head patterns could indicate genuinely different mechanism OR failure of Attention Synopsis method for distributed representations; paper inadequately distinguishes these; vector arithmetic evidence is indirect vs. RTE's strong head ablations

Generalization fundamentally unexamined: DiT-nano fails completely (5% accuracy), suggesting circuits emerge only at sufficient capacity, but why/when is unexplored; single architecture tested (PixArt); single pretrained encoder (T5-XXL) despite CLIP+T5 duals being common

Robustness analysis incomplete: only one perturbation type tested ('add the'); claims about T5 brittleness and encoder being bottleneck lack systematic support across paraphrasing, synonymy, reordering, and other linguistic variations

Mechanistic interpretability methodology gaps: aggregation sensitivity unquantified, no systematic multiple-comparison correction, causality claims from attention patterns alone exceed evidence standards (no surgical circuit interventions per Ferrando et al. 2024), faithfulness of ablations unclear

Actionability for practitioners absent: findings amount to 'T5 and random embeddings solve task differently'—no guidance on which approach scales, how to leverage insights to improve real systems, or what architectural changes follow from analysis

Limited scope of related work engagement with broader mechanistic interpretability (polysemanticity, superposition, circuits); T5-DiT circuit interpretation weakly justified—increased partial R² for relation (12%→21%) described as 'amplification' without confirming information preservation vs. transformation

strengths: Rigorous mechanistic circuit analysis with multiple validation approaches (ablation, intervention, QK analysis) showing concrete causal evidence for identified attention heads L2H8 and L4H3

Novel Attention Synopsis method that effectively manages and aggregates massive attention tensor spaces (>10 million maps) to identify functional patterns, with potential as a general tool for diffusion model analysis
Key insight that different text encoders (T5 vs. RTE) lead to fundamentally different circuits (modular vs. information fusion), with implications for text encoder design in future T2I models

Robustness analysis revealing that T5-DiT degrades dramatically with perturbations (+40% accuracy drop from adding 'the') while RTE-DiT is robust, exposing hidden brittleness despite similar in-domain performance

Thorough experimental validation across multiple model sizes (nano to DiT-B) with consistent findings, variance partitioning analysis showing how relation information is reorganized through DiT MLP, and vector arithmetic experiments demonstrating causal control of spatial relations
Well-designed controlled synthetic task with clear ground truth enabling rigorous mechanistic analysis; clear presentation with effective visualizations and reproducible methodology
weaknesses: Limited scope: toy synthetic task (2 objects, 3 shapes, 2 colors, 8 relations, 128×128 images) raises significant questions about generalization to complex scenes with multiple objects, diverse attributes, and real-world visual complexity

Unclear practical impact: paper provides mechanistic insights but proposes no concrete improvements to real T2I models or actionable guidance for practitioners on how to leverage findings for spatial relation improvements

T5-DiT analysis incomplete: authors acknowledge 'no clear pattern emerges from averaging' for attention-based analysis; T5-DiT findings rely on embedding analysis rather than mechanistic circuit understanding, making it less satisfying than RTE-DiT story

Evaluation method limitations: simple contour detection and color thresholding appropriate for shapes but brittle and non-scalable; no error bars or statistical significance testing on main results despite multiple random seeds

Missing critical ablations: no direct comparison of which architectural factors drive mechanistic differences (e.g., does T5 self-attention alone cause fusion, or is it the embedding structure?); no analysis of failure modes or robustness boundaries

No validation beyond toy setting: despite claims about real-world scenarios and practical difficulty of spatial relations, no evaluation on realistic prompts, real image datasets, or demonstration that insights improve actual T2I models

strengths: Novel mechanistic interpretability approach to spatial reasoning in DiTs with methodological innovations (Attention Synopsis, weight-space screening, variance partitioning)
Rigorous experimental design with controlled synthetic dataset, multiple model sizes, and comprehensive ablations with strong causal evidence
Clear circuit discoveries contrasting modular (RTE) vs. integrated (T5) strategies for encoding spatial relations, with direct explanation of robustness differences
Practical finding that T5-based models are brittle to prompt perturbations while RTE-based models are stable, relevant for T2I deployment
Reproducible research with comprehensive methodological details and promised public release of code/datasets
Generalizes analysis across encoders (T5, CLIP) and attempts transfer to pre-trained models
weaknesses: Extremely limited scope: toy synthetic dataset (3 shapes, 2 colors, 8 relations, 128×128px, 2 objects, gray backgrounds) orders of magnitude simpler than real T2I prompts with no evidence of scalability
Poor transfer to real models: PixArt-Sigma analysis shows only 8/30 object pairs have meaningful spatial accuracy, undercutting claims about understanding real T2I systems
RTE baseline is artificial—no real models use random embeddings; comparison against realistic encoders with semantic structure would be more informative than RTE
Circular analysis methods: Attention Synopsis relies on knowing true labels; object evaluation uses brittle pixel thresholding; weight-space screening depends on correct variance factorization
Limited actionability: identifies T5 brittleness (40% accuracy drop) without proposing solutions or tested interventions to improve spatial robustness
Speculative extrapolation to real-world scenarios (Abstract/Intro) contradicted by weak pre-trained model performance; findings may not generalize beyond synthetic setting
No analysis of scalability to 3+ objects, complex relations (occlusion, 'between'), or natural language variation; missing statistical confidence intervals and error bars
Presentation: critical methods relegated to appendix; figures are small/dense; narrative could better prioritize key findings for venue

strengths: Rigorous mechanistic interpretability study with novel analysis methods (Attention Synopsis, weight-space screening)
Well-designed controlled synthetic task enabling systematic comparison across model sizes and text encoders
Multiple converging evidence sources: attention analysis, ablations, causal interventions, and representational analysis
Clear mechanistic insights distinguishing RTE modular circuit from T5 information-fusion approach
Comprehensive experimental methodology with good documentation and reproducible setup
weaknesses: Task complexity is orders of magnitude simpler than real T2I (128×128, 3 shapes, 2 colors, 8 relations); generalization to practice highly uncertain
Critical validation failure: PixArt-Sigma shows poor spatial generation (8/30 object pairs), and token ablation contradicts synthetic findings, with inadequate explanation of this disconnect
No actionable improvements proposed for real models; abstract overstates practical applicability despite weak evidence for transfer
Findings are not particularly surprising (different architectures learn different solutions; attention correlates with position); limited novel insights
Limited scope: only PixArt architecture tested; cannot determine if findings are architecture-specific or reflect general principles
Causality claims could be stronger; interventions are somewhat artificial; no weight modification experiments
Robustness analysis limited to three specific perturbations; T5 brittleness is somewhat expected a priori given information fusion
Statistical rigor concerns: modest ablation effects, limited confidence intervals, no multiple comparison corrections despite screening many heads
Variance partitioning method concerns acknowledged but unresolved; sum-to-zero constraint introduces potential bias; no comparison to alternatives like sparse autoencoders
Pre-trained model analysis is insufficient given poor absolute performance; authors don't adequately explain why synthetic circuits fail to transfer

strengths: Novel mechanistic investigation of spatial relation generation in diffusion transformers, addressing an important gap between attention manipulation work and circuit understanding
Discovery of text-encoder-dependent circuits with strong empirical validation through multiple approaches (attention analysis, ablations, causal manipulation, vector arithmetic)

Important robustness finding: T5-based models brittle to prompt perturbations (~40% accuracy drop with minor changes) while RTE-based models robust, with clear mechanistic explanation via representation interference

Sophisticated methodological contributions: Attention Synopsis for analyzing massive attention tensors (~10M maps), weight-space screening for efficient head discovery, variance partitioning for representation analysis
Rigorous experimental design with controlled synthetic task, multiple model sizes, and systematic comparisons across text encoders (RTE, T5, CLIP)
Well-validated circuits: RTE-DiT's two-stage circuit clearly identified with strong ablation evidence (L2H8 alone accounts for 34% reduction in relational accuracy) and injection validation
Actionable insight that text embedding architecture may be more critical bottleneck than DiT modifications for spatial reasoning
Excellent presentation with clear figures (especially 4-7), comprehensive appendix (45 pages), pseudocode, and promised code/data release
weaknesses: Severely limited task scope: only 2 objects, simple geometric shapes (circle, square, triangle), 8 discrete spatial relations, 2 colors, 128×128 images—unclear if circuits scale to realistic multi-object compositions with complex objects and continuous spatial positioning

Weak transfer to real models: PixArt-Sigma analysis (A.10) shows only 8/30 object pairs achieve nontrivial accuracy, suggesting discovered circuits may not be relevant to complex real-world T2I systems

Incomplete mechanistic explanation: identifies what circuits exist but lacks explanation for why these specific circuits emerge; self-attention and MLP layers barely analyzed; questions of minimality and emergence unaddressed

T5 circuit interpretation has limitations: variance partitioning shows correlation but causality only tested via vector arithmetic; zero-sum constraint may introduce bias; uncertain whether discovered effect vectors capture actual computational structure or statistical artifacts

Generalizability of proposed methods unclear: Attention Synopsis tailored to this problem; weight-space screening assumes sinusoidal positional embeddings dominate (approximation); methods may not transfer to other architectures or tasks

Statistical rigor gaps: no formal significance testing reported despite visible variance in results; confidence intervals and permutation test results sparse; consistency across random seeds not assessed
Evaluation based on simple 5-pixel tolerances and 8-pixel 'loose' margins may oversimplify spatial reasoning complexity; object parsing via intensity thresholding potentially brittle
No demonstration of how insights improve real T2I systems: cannot fix spatial failures in production models; unclear practical implications beyond text encoder design guidance
